reviews.text: Excellent service.

I highly recommend it, surgical center, semi-intensive care, ward, service, team of clinical professionals 100%

The price is steep; but it was worth every penny.

I'd like to share my experience... my little dog, Snow, needed an MRI and we took him to Veros. I'm so glad I made that choice after doing some research. When we arrived at the hospital, I noticed the excellent service from reception to going upstairs for the actual exam. The cleanliness was impeccable, the nurses explained the whole procedure which put me at ease, everything went super well and Snow came out looking like he hadn't even had the exam. Thank you so much for the care and professionalism, don't hesitate to take your dog there.
Good facilities, good service, and quality when it comes to pet care.

We took our dog to the hospital looking for a neurologist. As is typical of these emergency rooms, they immediately wanted to push us towards a consultation with an ER doctor and then add the cost of the neurologist... anyway... she saw a neurologist, Dr. Rebeca, a very good doctor by the way, however, her care is far below what a clinic of that size offers.
We felt extremely cheated, we had a problem with the issuance of a prescription, but the doctor herself was not at fault because a hospital of that size DOES NOT ISSUE THAT TYPE OF PRESCRIPTION, and for the absurd prices they charge, I found it totally out of line. My dog ​​was without medication for a long time due to this poor organization. Their after-sales service is terrible, we don't feel safe recommending them or continuing treatment. There is something very impersonal about it, in our view, they just want to receive payment and send you to many things, without first studying the clinical case. I do not recommend it and would not return to the place.

The service at this place is terrible!
It took them 4 hours to tell me what day and time the vet works!
A place that charges an exorbitant, unrealistic price, with such terrible service!
I started the service at 10:25 AM and they only responded at 2:20 PM!
Unacceptable. It's like the public health system!
Now, I've been trying to schedule an appointment for almost half an hour since it's the only place she works where I can get a day and time to go, and nobody answers.
The lame excuse? High volume!
High volume for the receptionist?
Yeah, right!

I would like to commend veterinarian Davi Ferreira.
Davi admitted my dog, Baltazar, to the emergency room with extreme calm, ethical conduct, and confidence. It was very evident that he possesses technical skills, the ability to communicate difficult news, and the expertise to handle emergency situations. The other veterinarian who arrived for the emergency care was also very professional; I apologize, I don't recall her name.

I am a geriatrician and palliative care physician, and I work in geriatric emergency settings. I teach my residency students how to maintain a technical and compassionate approach to emergency scenarios in humans.
I was very impressed and proud to see a healthcare professional like Davi handling our family with such competence—after all, dogs are our family.
Indeed, the initial care makes all the difference, whether in human or veterinary medicine.

Please pass this praise on to Davi:
Davi, may you continue to improve yourself, study, and love what you do! Never forget your worth and your calling. I will always remember your generous and confident gaze in the emergency room; I will be eternally grateful to you.

I also thank the treasury staff, Edi and Alane, for their welcoming attitude, cordiality, and explanations during payments.

I thank the veterinarians Gabriela, Tamires, and Isabela, with whom I had contact during visits to Baltazar in the ICU - for their affection and attentive and enlightening communication, in addition to providing detailed information on the app.

I thank veterinarian Julia Braga who cared for my other dog in the emergency room with such zeal and affection.

Gratitude!

Everything was perfect. From scheduling to my cat Chica's discharge. We scheduled the CT scan via WhatsApp (we received excellent service). On the day, at the hospital, they offer valet parking; the attendant greets you and immediately puts on the pet's companion ID. Then we were taken to the 2nd floor where the CT and MRI exams are performed. They took us to the pet waiting area, which was completely calm with Feliway. My cat was super relaxed. Then the nurse came to talk and explain how the anesthesia would be administered, its duration, etc. We handed over Chica, and the exam started exactly at 12:30 pm, the scheduled time. We went to lunch, and when we returned, the attendant gave us the news that everything had gone well and Chica was eating in the recovery room. At 2 pm she was discharged, and we went home. They delivered her clean, with a bow, and changed the bandages on her esophageal tube. I can only thank everyone on this team who welcomed us so well. Congratulations, Veros Vet.

My dissatisfaction with the clinic's service

Yesterday we were at the clinic with our dog, Bandeirinha, who underwent an evaluation with a veterinary neurologist after experiencing several seizures.

After the consultation and pain medication, we received a prescription for Cronidor 40 mg, with instructions that we could buy the medication at smaller pharmacies or pet shops.

The problem started this morning when we needed to administer the medication at 8 am and discovered that the prescription was not suitable for purchase.

We tried to find the medication in several establishments, without success.

We contacted the clinic at 8:30 am, but only received an effective solution around 3:30 pm, after being informed that there had been an error in the prescription.

Our dog was only able to take the medication at 4 pm.

**How ​​can a clinic of this size take so many hours to resolve a situation caused by an internal error?**

** ... There was a lack of communication, organization, and speed in resolving a problem that directly affected our dog's treatment.

The minimum expected would have been that the correct prescription had been provided from the beginning or that an alternative had been prepared to avoid this problem.

We spent a fortune on yesterday's appointment and expected support of that caliber, especially at a time when we were so concerned about our dog's health.

It's not just about the mistake, but about the delay and difficulty in communicating how to correct it.

*This serves as our warning and expresses our deep dissatisfaction. When it comes to an animal's health, time, responsibility, and service make all the difference.

My first experience at Veros was very good from beginning to end.
We had a CT scan, surgery, and hospitalization. The service, cleanliness of the place, the facilities, the clarity, the examination, the pre- and post-operative care—everything was perfect, without any points of concern. We were well received and attended to; we felt cared for from the reception, from the coffee break to the check-out. And they were so kind to my dog. Without a doubt, it gave me a lot of confidence. Based on my experience and everything in my opinion, I highly recommend it!
Fantastic. Service, care, and skill of the professionals, 1000 out of 1000!!
Care and attention for pets ❤️

Don't be fooled by the sophisticated appearance. Perhaps it's a result of prioritizing the bill as their number one priority. When we really needed them, we were let down. The on-call doctor who treated us was extremely rude and impatient. There are much better and fairer options available. I'll stay far away.
Easy access, with on-site parking, a snack bar, and pets are very well taken care of.

My experience with the clinic was marked by two quite distinct aspects.

I was very well attended to by the on-call veterinarian in the early morning of August 31st, around 4 am. She was attentive, professional, and showed care during the treatment of my dog.

Unfortunately, I did not have the same impression of the two nurses who were on duty. I perceived a lack of preparedness that I consider incompatible with a private, reputable clinic located in an area like Jardins.

I even had difficulties with the way my dog ​​was immobilized. Furthermore, as he was undergoing treatment for alopecia, I explained that I did not want his fur shaved. The professionals' reaction to my instructions, with expressions and gestures that showed evident displeasure, was quite unpleasant and unnecessary.

As a pet owner, I hope that my observations about an animal under my care will be heard with respect and professionalism, especially in an emergency situation during the early morning hours.

I'm leaving this note not to disparage the clinic, especially since the veterinarian who treated us was excellent, but to emphasize that the team's standard of care needs to be consistent at all levels. A clinic with such a good reputation should offer not only good facilities, but also well-trained, caring, and respectful professionals, both for pet owners and, above all, for the animals.

We had an MRI scan performed on our puppy to investigate a possible cervical disc herniation diagnosis with Dr. Isabela at Veros, and we are so grateful for all the care, affection, and attention they gave him throughout the entire procedure.

We are very happy and relieved with how he was treated. It's a high-tech hospital with excellent facilities and, most importantly, extremely humane, attentive, and kind professionals.

Our sincerest thanks to Dr. Isabela and the entire Veros team for taking such good care of our Bucky!
State-of-the-art veterinary hospital

I am writing to inform other pet owners of the negative experience we had at Veros, so it is up to the pet owner to decide whether or not to submit to such disrespect.
My dog ​​needed surgery and we were referred to Samantha, from the Veros team. All services were extremely expensive but with the guarantee of high-standard treatment. We were very dissatisfied with all communication from the hospital, hours without news of the animal, the official chat constantly giving an error (attached) and not receiving any answers. We tried calling the hospital's landline, which is supposed to be 24 hours, but the ICU extension was constantly busy, I imagine disconnected. At reception, the phone just rang without anyone answering, and the calls on other extensions dropped.

A great lack of consideration for the customer.

Another detail was on the day of discharge when, unlike previous days when payment was settled upon departure, upon discharge the dog is held hostage by the hospital and they don't let you go upstairs before settling the remaining amount.
We had already paid around 6,000 to the hospital and another 4,000 to Samantha, and we still owed around 1,500 for antibiotics and surgical mesh, which is a very small amount for such distrust and disrespectful treatment.
We also didn't like having an unknown veterinarian giving post-operative instructions instead of Samantha herself, whom we had hired.
We don't mind paying a lot to have the best treatment for our pet, but we demand respect and consideration for pet owners. Much smaller and less well-known clinics offer more humane treatment than Veros.
I was contacted by Danielle Silveira, Veros' quality director, and at no point was there an apology or retraction of what happened. This is because it wasn't an exception, but rather protocol.

I do not recommend them.

They provide a WhatsApp number, but no one answers. I spoke with the customer service representative, informed her that I wasn't getting a response, and she didn't seem to care much. Since I knew there would be several questions and requests for information, WhatsApp makes things easier.
I've been waiting for two hours to be seen! The doctor left the office to attend to an emergency and no one came back to talk to me! Terrible service! Worst veterinary hospital in São Paulo.

I would like to register the terrible experience I had at the hospital today!! I had scheduled tests for my dog ​​at 2 PM, we arrived on time, went up to the floor we were directed to, and informed the reception that we were there to have coagulation profile tests, ultrasound-guided thoracentesis, and a CT scan done. We waited for an hour with a 90kg dog who had been fasting for 12 hours! After questioning the delay and requesting an explanation from the staff, the reception said our appointment was at 3:30 PM, completely wrong information that demonstrates the staff's lack of communication and preparedness! When we showed the 2 PM appointment confirmation, we received no response from reception, showing that they had no interest in correcting their mistake and providing good service! A complete lack of respect for the animal. Furthermore, they sent all the other pets who arrived later to have their tests done ahead of us, which leads one to believe that they were indeed delaying the dog's exam because of his size! It is worth noting that we requested a report from the anesthesia team to provide the dog's complete medical history, and we have not received this response.

We were very worried about our Shih Tzu's health, as she became very ill during the early hours of the morning on a holiday! But we were pleasantly surprised to be treated by the excellent professional Dr. Lucas Sanchez, who provided prompt care and meticulously guided us through the treatment. Today she is doing very well! I can only praise the doctor's care as well as the facilities at Veros Hospital!
Great experience. Very good service and excellent facilities.
Very friendly and competent, a well-trained team and facilities that are unparalleled in the world of veterinary medicine. Congratulations and thank you very much.

I had an extremely frustrating and painful experience with Veros during my dog ​​Pingo's hospitalization and post-operative period.

He underwent surgery on September 1st and remained hospitalized. During this time, I received practically no information spontaneously and had to constantly request updates through the app. When I asked objective questions, such as whether he had eaten, drunk water, urinated, or taken his medication, I basically received the response that he was "stable." For a pet owner with a hospitalized animal, this is insufficient.

On September 2nd, when I went to visit him, I discovered that he hadn't eaten. I brought fruit, and he ate with me and drank plenty of water. If I had received this information earlier, I would have gone to the hospital much sooner.

He also needed blood tests and an ultrasound, but these tests were not performed during his hospitalization. The justification given was the high number of animals hospitalized.

In the following days, Pingo continued to be lethargic and worsened. We returned to Veros via the emergency room, where he received treatment and was discharged. At the emergency room, he waited two hours to be seen. No one triaged him to assess the severity of his condition. He was unwell the entire time.

The following day, we had the requested tests done. In the afternoon, as his condition worsened, we sought treatment at another hospital. He was evaluated, medicated, and admitted, but he died en route, just minutes before we arrived.

After his death, tests showed that he was developing post-operative kidney failure. What angers me is that, throughout this entire process, there was no suspicion or warning from Veros regarding this, nor the follow-up I expected from a veterinary hospital.

I also had a problem with a charge related to Cerenia. I authorized the application through Veros Chat, but my authorization hadn't even been viewed. When I questioned the charge, they went to look for the authorization, and only then did the message appear as read. I requested a refund, and it was not processed.

I paid for all the treatment privately precisely because I wanted to offer my dog ​​the best possible care. Unfortunately, I left with the feeling that I had to beg for basic information while my dog ​​was hospitalized.

I know that not every animal survives, even with proper treatment. My criticism isn't simply because Pingo died. It's because of the lack of communication, follow-up, transparency, and support throughout the entire process.

It was a very painful experience and, unfortunately, I don't intend to take my other pets to Veros anymore.

Want to schedule an appointment? Wait at least 4 months and pay 600 reais for a 10-minute consultation.
Oh! Want a discount on Pix? It's not 7% ​​anymore, it's 3%.
Top notch, very good, even more so with the professional Igor Domingues working there, a person who puts a lot of love and care into what he does.
The veterinary care is amazing, but the requirement to leave the car with the valet even when there are parking spaces in front seems unfair to me.

Top-notch hospital. My pet and I received excellent care. Valet parking and the facility has all the latest amenities. Clean, organized, and with excellent professionals.
They offer boarding for pets along with their owners, which makes all the difference.
I highly recommend Veros' facilities.

This is, without a doubt, the most difficult assessment I've ever had to make.

My dog ​​had been a neurological patient at Veros Hospital for years. In 2024, he underwent surgery there to remove a tumor, and since then, all his follow-up, exams, and treatments have been done at the hospital. Therefore, Veros became our trusted hospital.

Last Sunday, after months without seizures, he had an extremely aggressive one. Following the advice of his neurologist, we immediately went to Veros for emergency care and hospitalization.

He was taken to the emergency room and, due to the severity of the seizures, needed to be sedated. Up to that point, I have no complaints about the care.

What happened next, however, was devastating.

When we tried to admit him to the ICU, we were informed that there were no beds available. Even given the severity of his condition, the sedation, and his entire history as a patient at the hospital, the only alternative presented was his transfer to another hospital in an ambulance.

We questioned whether there wasn't any other possibility of keeping him there, considering his critical condition. The answer was no.

We paid approximately R$1,000.00 for an ambulance to travel about 200 meters. My dog ​​was inside it for approximately two minutes.

Upon arriving at the other hospital, we discovered that he had aspirated during the seizures and already had lung damage. Shortly afterward, he passed away.

And this is a question that will haunt us forever: if he had been admitted, hospitalized, and investigated immediately at the hospital that had been following his entire history, could the outcome have been different?

I can't say for sure. But we'll never have that answer either.

It's devastating to lose an animal that was part of our family. And it's even more painful to know that, at the moment when we most needed the hospital we trusted for years, we were forced to look for another because there was no space to receive him.

My dog ​​wasn't just another patient. He had a history at that hospital.

Today, in addition to the immense pain of loss, there remains the feeling that, at a critical moment, the lack of resources and a bed may have cost him the chance to stay alive.

We lost our dog. And, along with him, we also lost all the trust we built up over the years in Veros Hospital.

Lack of transparency and inhumanity towards the consumer. My dog ​​underwent surgery and was then hospitalized for post-operative care, and I faced successive billing errors and undue charges for services not performed.

I am writing to express my profound indignation, outrage, and pain at the commercial, mechanical, and negligent attitude of the medical team at Veros's hospitalization facility.

However, the worst and most inhumane thing happened on my son's last day of life, Saturday (August 29, 2026). During the midday visit, I found him in a shocking and desperate state: he was extremely restless, unable to stand, with a vacant stare fixed on the wall, drooling thick, abundant, and sticky saliva all over his mouth, in addition to involuntarily defecating all over his body. When I desperately questioned the on-call veterinarian about this deplorable state, the medical team negligently minimized the situation, stating that it was "just severe nausea and reflux" caused by slow bowel movements. The on-call staff hid the true severity of the situation from me and proposed that I immediately undergo new, expensive, and aggressive procedures: another urgent exploratory surgery on his abdomen, the possible administration of blood transfusions, and switching to a highly risky antibiotic. The truth only came to light because I demanded the release of the blood test results in the system. The biochemical report released at 2:44 PM that same day revealed what the medical team had tried to hide in order to continue making money: my dog's liver had gone into acute failure (Bilirubin skyrocketed to 9.00 mg/dL and AST rising) and his blood was severely intoxicated (Phosphorus skyrocketed to 8.1 mg/dL). That abundant, sticky drool and vacant stare were classic symptoms of Hepatic Encephalopathy (brain intoxication due to liver failure), and not just simple nausea.

The hospital operated in a completely commercial and mechanical way. They knew, through lab tests, that his little body had reached its absolute limit and that any further surgery or heavy medication would be pointless cruelty. Even so, they omitted the real diagnosis of liver failure and tried to push invasive procedures on me, preferring to prolong my animal's suffering until exhaustion and total collapse in the early morning to inflate the hospital bill. If I hadn't had the intuition to read the tests myself and confront the team demanding euthanasia to end my son's agony, they would have cut my dog ​​open again on an operating table in a completely inhumane way. Veros has a luxurious physical structure, but the clinical leadership on duty demonstrated a frightening lack of empathy, ethics, and transparency.

They treat lives like lucrative medical records. Unfortunately, many other animals will go through this, will be treated to the point of exhaustion, many of us pet owners will not know the truth, and we will leave Veros with huge amounts of money and without our children. Don't trust, don't take, don't leave at this hospital.

Besides everything else, my deepest gratitude to everyone who stayed by my side all these days: the girls from the cafeteria, the cleaning staff, the valet parking attendants, the receptionists, Diego and Thamires from the treasury, and a very special person who hugged us when we said goodbye to our little one, the nurse Fábio Magalhães, a humane person who deserves all our gratitude.

Two and a half hours waiting in line at the emergency room.
Bizarre.
Excellent service from Dr. Catarina.
Very good!
My dog ​​had an MRI at this veterinary hospital, which has an excellent facility.
Excellent veterinary hospital. Polite and caring staff. Prices are high but worth it.

The service, from the valets to the reception, was all attentive, however, my dog ​​went in for an exam on August 16th at 1 AM, had a seizure while they were trying to get him back from the exam, I had to transfer him to another hospital and admit him to the ICU!! Today, August 19th, 2026
After 3 days he passed away!

The detail is that he was only 5 years old and I have doubts about the procedure performed after the exam!! After reading the entire process performed with him at Veros, I believe he could be alive!! I am extremely dissatisfied with this institution, I will not return and I do not recommend it!!
Best veterinary hospital ever!! Excellent service, highly qualified professionals.

My experience at the Veterinary Hospital was simply exceptional, and I want to leave this testimonial especially to thank Dr. Fernanda, the endoscopist.

My cat, Theo, had been bleeding for about 2 years and, during that time, he went to several specialists and underwent different evaluations, without us being able to discover the cause of the problem. Then we met Dr. Fernanda, who, with great competence and attention, promptly identified the cause and managed to solve the problem.

In addition to her technical excellence, Dr. Fernanda's care was impeccable and extremely humane. She showed great care, explained the entire process clearly, and conveyed a great sense of security throughout the treatment. After so long trying to find out what was happening to Theo, I finally had an answer and, most importantly, a solution.

I would also like to praise the entire team and the hospital's facilities, which are magnificent. We were very well treated at every stage, from reception, through the procedure, to post-procedure follow-up. During a time of such concern for a pet that is part of our family, being welcomed in this way made all the difference.

My gratitude to Dr. Fernanda and the entire hospital team. Theo is doing very well, and I have no words to thank them for finally discovering and resolving a problem that had been bothering us for so long.

Pathetic and completely misguided service at the ER, from beginning to end. Confusing, wrong, and inconclusive diagnosis, and it wasn't the first time I've experienced this there. Overpriced tests and incomplete reports… In short, it's also my fault, as I insisted on going to this MONEY-MAKING MACHINE more than once, since this "hospital" is nothing more than that. Lack of ethics and professional qualification is also abundant there. Be careful and open your eyes, you risk harming your pet's health instead of improving it, and you'll spend a lot of money doing so at this place. If I hadn't rushed to get a second opinion at another clinic the next day, my dog ​​might not even be here anymore… Luckily, I left Veros completely insecure and dissatisfied, and quickly found another veterinarian elsewhere.

All of my appointments with Camila Ferreiro were canceled at least once; one appointment was canceled three times. A serious lack of commitment to clients. We plan all the exams to be seen in time for the follow-up appointment, only to have them canceled later.

The service is very good, but everything there is excessive, including the cost.
It seems more like a human hospital than a pet hospital. I find it exaggerated and unnecessary.

I had an MRI done on my pet, and I just want to thank the entire parking lot team, the reception, the anesthesiologist, the assistants—everyone was impeccable and very professional. I felt safe, calm, and welcomed, and my pet was very well taken care of.
The service is excellent, from reception to the medical staff. I took my 15-year-old dog to see the neurologist; she's a very good, sensible, and attentive doctor.
Excellent hospital. Very well equipped, first-rate service, and they even have delicious coffee.
Excellent!
Beautiful, clean hospital with excellent service, from reception to healthcare professionals.

Unfortunately, I had to end my relationship with the hospital, even after they cared for two of my cats. I scheduled an appointment, and just because I didn't check WhatsApp, they took the liberty of canceling it, leaving me and my sick cat without care. I'm very sad to end my relationship with the hospital like this, but denying scheduled care to a sick animal is absurd.
Professional and attentive service.

I've always taken my dogs to Veros and always had good experiences. Unfortunately, the visit on July 20th, 2026 was extremely concerning.

After a simple auscultation, the veterinarian stated that my dog ​​had significant pulmonary edema and a heart murmur, immediately recommending arterial blood gas analysis, blood tests, X-rays, and starting treatment with furosemide and dexamethasone, even before confirming the diagnosis.

Even after a quick ultrasound and the X-ray itself, she continued to claim that the lung was "full of fluid" and insisted that I start treatment. Fortunately, I decided to wait for the official report before medicating my dog.

The next day, the radiographic report ruled out pulmonary edema, describing lungs without relevant alterations and a heart with preserved dimensions.

I wonder how many pet owners would agree to undergo arterial blood gas analysis—an invasive and painful exam—and start treatment with diuretics and corticosteroids relying solely on the assessment received. If I had followed the hospital's instructions, my dog ​​would have undergone an invasive procedure and been treated for a disease that, according to the hospital's own report, did not exist.

I don't question the possibility of raising diagnostic hypotheses, but I consider it very serious to present a hypothesis as certainty and insist on treatment before confirmation by tests. I hope the hospital reconsiders this conduct so that other patients do not go through the same situation.

My cat was admitted to the emergency room and hospitalized for 2 days. She returned for surgery the following week and stayed for another 2 days. After being discharged 2 days later, she returned on a Saturday to spend the entire week and passed away on Sunday! I spoke with the doctor, Dr. Ricardo K. Shimizu (Xicá), who performed the first surgery on her that day, before and after the surgery, and never again, even though she returned to the hospital after being discharged and the ICU recommended another surgery. He told another doctor to do it because it was Saturday. When I left the hospital on Sunday, devastated by the death of my cat, who initially only needed to have her gallbladder removed and a biopsy of her intestine, I answered a questionnaire saying that everything was fine, but today, thinking about everything that happened, I see that it wasn't. Tomorrow, July 21st, marks one month since she died, and nothing will bring her back. In total, I spent the equivalent of a mid-range car, since she was there for 12 days, the last 2 in the ICU, and only the doctors in the ward spoke to me (and each day it was a different doctor). All I heard was that she had an inflammation and that it worsened until her death. At no point did I refuse any exam or procedure. I authorized everything that was requested, including the second surgery under absolute pressure from the ICU doctor, who sent me the surgery paperwork at 6:28 PM and by 6:33 PM was already asking me if she could proceed. Today I feel I should have fought harder for her; I was resilient, thinking she was in a good hospital, but that doesn't absolve the medical responsibility of the surgeon who should have spoken to me to explain what was happening and what the options were. In short, nothing will bring my little girl back, but this serves as my record that a beautiful hospital and super cordial service from all the staff are not enough when dealing with lives. Just a heartfelt message from someone who managed to think rationally the day before the one-month anniversary of my sweet Paçoca's death!

The hospital is extremely well-equipped and modern.
The medical team and staff are extremely polite and helpful.
I recommend it without any doubt.

Hello,

Thank you very much for your feedback, you can always count on us!

A hug from the entire Veros team.

(11) 3900-7000 - Options 1 - 5 and 2 (call)
(11) 94107-9961 - Customer Service Option (WhatsApp)
A distinguished veterinary hospital with excellent service and top-notch facilities.
The medical staff provided very attentive service and were all very polite. The price is high.

The hospital has a fantastic structure; I've never seen anything like it for pet care, and very competent professionals like Dr. Júlia in the ER. That said, my dog ​​had a case of gastroenteritis and had to be hospitalized, and from then on, despite knowing it's an expensive hospital, the abuses become apparent. They try in every way to push "extremely necessary" tests on you, which, after talking to my dog's veterinarian, she told me weren't really necessary. Another point to lament is the app they use to communicate with the families of hospitalized pets; it's a shame, it seems like something from the 90s, messages take a long time to load, audio doesn't load. Therefore, despite the good structure and professionals, it's not worth what they charge, especially since they charge indiscriminately.
Excellent. Great attention and dedication to the animals.

Since experiencing discomfort at another service (where I had my cats' routine checkups and went when I needed urgent care), I've become more wary of these services.
During this time, I ended up looking for more information about feline care.
So far, I've only gone to Veros to have one of my kittens' exams done.
I received excellent service from the Customer Service Center until the payment was finalized.
The professionals were excellent with my kitten.
Congratulations to the entire team!
I believe the CEO is very good, because I've noticed that whoever is at the top of the pyramid makes a big difference in the service we receive (I say this in all sectors - at reception, in the hallways, in the exam rooms...)

The hospital's facilities are incredible. The service is extremely attentive – from arrival in the parking lot to departure. I arrived with my weak dog, and everyone helped us and was very caring towards her.
Excellent facilities, I found all the specialists I was looking for there!!
Good location

Veros is an amazing hospital with an extremely competent team. The specialist veterinarians are wonderful (especially Dr. Ana Paula, my cat's nephrologist) and the nursing staff is super skilled and caring. It is expensive, yes, but they have already saved my elderly renal cat's life 3 times (and I hope she continues to be here for a long time), so it's something I'm very grateful for.
My cat has chronic kidney disease and is being monitored by Dr. Ana P. Reis, a nephrologist. The care and support are excellent! Dr. Ana is great 🙏 …
Excellent service, very clean and organized place, and quick service.

Hello,

Thank you very much for your feedback, you can always count on us!

A hug from the entire Veros team.

(11) 3900-7000 - Options 1 - 5 and 2 (call)
(11) 94107-9961 - Customer Service Option (WhatsApp)
Great Veterinarian Saved My Cat

Veros has a very serious problem with incompetence in the administrative area. The simplest part of a veterinary hospital would be scheduling, but they can't even do that right.
I had more than two negative experiences in one week in this regard. First, it's a mess for online consultations. It's a nightmare to schedule, as it requires the "leader" to be present at the consultation, in addition to the veterinarian and the owner. Therefore, you would expect that this person to be useful, but no! I waited 45 minutes and only because I called did I find out that the veterinarian had to attend to a serious patient (she was doing her job) and NO ONE from scheduling/leadership had the decency to let me know. The vet was busy doing her job, but those responsible for scheduling forgot about the consultation. A chaos!
In the very same week, a procedure was scheduled for my dog. I never changed the time of this procedure, nor the date. They sent me a message the day before confirming with the correct time (9 am). Upon arriving, after waiting for 1 hour and 20 minutes, I inquired if they would admit my dog ​​immediately, as he was fasting. They told me the procedure was scheduled for 10:30 AM, so the wait was justified. Seriously??? Do they think the owner goes there with their dog fasting 2 hours and 30 minutes before the procedure because they find it fun and have nothing better to do??? I was still waiting for the anesthesiologist when two women from the coordination team arrived, acting like I looked like a fool, to give me that lame excuse. An apology doesn't fix the incompetence that prevails in the administration of this hospital! How can I expect them to take good care of my dog ​​if they can't even manage a simple appointment? And they made a fool of me twice in one week. I canceled the procedure and took my dog ​​out of there immediately! It was a sign that I won't leave my pets in the hands of an establishment that can't manage something so basic. INCOMPETENCE!

I would like to register my dissatisfaction with the service provided by Hospital Veros regarding the scheduling of a CT scan for my cat.
I contacted the hospital on the recommendation of two specialist doctors who are following his case. Upon contacting them, I was informed that there was availability for the CT scan for the following day (June 13th). Initially, the service was excellent. The team identified the absence of a necessary exam and informed me that it would be possible to schedule this procedure for the same day as the CT scan.
After the conversation ended, the team contacted me again to inquire about an alteration in my cat's kidney function. I explained that he has chronic kidney disease and has been undergoing treatment since October 2025. I also informed them that the responsible nephrologist had issued a letter stating that the patient was stable and cleared to undergo the exam. In addition, the blood count had been performed on May 26th, within the required timeframe of up to 30 days before the procedure.
After receiving this information, I was informed that everything was resolved and that the scheduling could proceed normally. I even asked twice if any additional preparation would be necessary beyond the 12-hour food fast and the 4-hour water fast. On both occasions, I received confirmation that there were no further instructions or requirements.
My cat is rigorously monitored for his health condition. He undergoes clinical follow-up twice a week for the administration of medications related to kidney function and monthly consultations with a nephrologist. Recently, during surgery, a tumor was identified and removed. Since then, we have started follow-up with an oncologist. Despite chemotherapy, there is suspicion of disease progression, which is why the three doctors responsible for the case (clinician, nephrologist, and oncologist) authorized and recommended a CT scan to assess the cancer's progression.
On the day of the exam, the CT scan was scheduled for 9:30 am. However, due to the need for a prior echocardiogram, we were instructed to arrive at the hospital at 8:30 am. When we were already on our way, the team contacted us. I received two calls that were immediately disconnected the moment I answered. Only after I returned the call and sent a message did I receive the explanation that the exam would need to be rescheduled.
The justification given was that fluid therapy would be necessary before the CT scan, a procedure that should take place approximately three hours in advance. However, this information was never mentioned during the scheduling process, even after the team had been informed in detail about the patient's kidney condition and even after my specific questions about the necessary preparation.
I consider this situation a complete disregard. If fluid therapy was considered essential to protect the patient's kidney function during the exam, this need should have been identified and communicated from the first contact. It is extremely concerning that a chronic kidney patient was unnecessarily subjected to a long period of food and water fasting due to a communication failure on the part of the institution itself.
Even more serious is the fact that the hospital had all the relevant clinical information in advance and had several opportunities to correctly guide the family and plan the procedure. It is expected that a specialized institution, especially when dealing with patients in delicate and complex conditions, will have adequate protocols and attention to detail necessary to ensure the safety and well-being of the animals.

Given all the disruption caused, the unnecessary exposure of the patient to fasting, and the evident failure of communication and organization, I would like to register my deep dissatisfaction with the care provided.

You call the hospital and get a recording saying it's the most complete place for your pet. Then you send a referral from the vet to administer medications and discover that the hospital doesn't administer any of the four medications the vet prescribed. Very complete indeed… 0 out of 10.

I took my puppy Oliver to have an MRI. I didn't know the hospital; I went on the recommendation of the veterinary orthopedist who is taking care of my puppy.

All the employees, from all sectors, are top-notch.

I can only thank the entire Veros team for their care and affection towards Tata. Unfortunately, her journey has come to an end, but everyone was extremely attentive and professional with us. Thank you to the exam results team and the finance team! You were incredible.

This hospital made a difficult moment even worse.

There are professionals who bring light in difficult times.

Unfortunately, my experience at the Veros veterinary hospital was the opposite.

During one of the most painful moments of our lives, when I made it clear that I wanted to stay by my dog's side as she passed away, the night shift director, Leia Guesser, responded in a mocking tone in front of her team:

- "Here, decisions need to be made rationally, not emotionally."

I agree that the procedure should be done rationally, but instead of understanding, we experienced coldness and a lack of empathy in the face of a family's suffering after losing a pet.

Not to mention that, while my dog ​​was in critical condition and her team couldn't understand the diagnosis, the doctor insisted on signing contracts and budgets.

Five contracts were signed in about 30 minutes.

And when I crossed paths with the doctor at the hospital after learning of my dog's irreversible condition, she walked right past me, keeping her distance. My experience was extremely disappointing. I invested around R$4,000 in the service and traveled over 400 km seeking specialized care for my dog ​​with meningoencephalitis, expecting not only technical competence but also empathy and responsibility—and I didn't find that.

Besides not receiving adequate explanations about the diagnosis and the severity of the condition, there was a lack of basic compassion and care at a critical moment. The most serious issue was that, in an emergency situation, when seeking urgent help, I only received the response that the professional was already attending to another patient, without any concern about whether my dog ​​was alive, how she was doing, or what measures had been taken. The clinic has an impressive structure and a reputation built over time, but structure alone does not sustain good service. Physical and historical excellence is useless when empathy, a sense of urgency, and a real commitment to the patient are lacking. Based on my experience, the quality of service fell far short of what the cost and reputation promised.

Our experience at the Veros veterinary clinic was disappointing, especially considering its reputation and the high prices charged.

Yesterday we went there urgently with our dog, and we chose this clinic precisely because of its excellent reputation, expecting high-quality service. However, this was not reflected in practice.

We paid an emergency fee (over R$1,000), but still waited more than an hour just to have an ultrasound. During that time, they informed us that no one was available to perform the ultrasound at that moment; they said there was a professional, but she was already outside of her hours. One of the doctors even acknowledged that our waiting time was excessive and apologized, but the fee was still charged.

During the wait, I asked a doctor in the hallway for help after a long time without information. I was respectful and only asked about the delay; I was desperate because every minute was crucial. However, this same professional later acted completely inappropriately: when I went to say goodbye to my dog ​​before the endoscopy, she reprimanded me out of nowhere!!! saying that I couldn't "rush" the team, that other patients were also urgent, and that I needed to understand the deadlines. It was completely out of context, lacking empathy, and at the worst possible moment, when my baby was about to undergo the procedure.

Another serious problem was at the time of payment—more than R$10,000 (without surgery, only endoscopy, x-ray, blood test, and ultrasound). We informed them that we had health insurance, and they told us it couldn't be used because we hadn't mentioned it upon arrival. At no point were we asked about this. In an emergency situation, it's absurd to expect the client to prioritize this type of information. Just because we didn't mention this upon arrival, we had to pay much more money.

On a positive note, we highlight the excellent endoscopy doctor, whose care was excellent, professional, and very humane; we are very grateful to her. Furthermore, we also received excellent service from the entire reception team (including security and receptionists), who were extremely attentive, concerned, and welcoming throughout the entire process. Also from the two Julias.

The clinic's infrastructure is incredible, but the treatment of some people, their handling of the situation, and their lack of empathy leave much to be desired considering the high prices charged.

I went to the hospital to have a Holter monitor test done. Veros' price is the highest on the market in São Paulo (it's almost three times that of Dognostico, and double that of Provet). Why would anyone pay so much for a test? Because the Holter monitor is a cardiac exam, and the report is extremely important for treating cases of bradycardia like my animal's, who recently underwent hospitalization because of it. And Veros, when selling you the exam, says that the report will be ready in 72 consecutive hours (I have this in writing), a shorter time than other places. And that's because they manage to get you to pull the fast one.
The problem is that they don't deliver on time. They simply don't deliver and don't give any explanation. I've been on WhatsApp for two hours trying to understand when I'm going to receive this report. I've already called customer service. Nothing.
I'm leaving here the comment that I wish I had read before paying so much for an exam that simply doesn't come out on time: it's not worth paying triple, it's not worth it because Veros simply doesn't deliver on time.
The issue is: even though it's late, I need this report!! It's essential for my dog's treatment.

LACK OF ETHICS. Service driven by financial interest.
I took my cat there because it was the closest option and because he was in a lot of pain.

Another clinic had already made a referral minutes before for an ultrasound, and if he had petrified feces, he should be hospitalized and undergo surgery.
The vet who did the ultrasound was wonderful, careful, and attentive. Because it was around 10 PM, I opted to have a consultation there so they could medicate him. I waited for over an hour to be seen; they claimed there was an emergency in the ICU. The consultation itself was fine, but they wanted to hospitalize my cat (unnecessarily), perform several tests and procedures (even though he was in pain), and I was against it. They said that since it was a referral, they would charge me a lower price for the consultation so that I would leave him hospitalized and have all the tests and procedures done that the clinic wanted.

I had already received another recommendation from another vet that I could take him home, medicate him, and administer sachets, and if he didn't defecate within 48 hours, it would be necessary to take him in for an enema. I chose not to hospitalize him because there was indeed no need, but they insisted, claiming that the vet had referred him for hospitalization, and I countered that hospitalization was only IF it was surgical. In that case, the clinic informed me that since I wouldn't leave him hospitalized, they would charge me the full consultation fee. I questioned the vet, and she said it was the manager's instruction. The vet said I was entitled to a follow-up appointment within 48 hours, even though it's up to 30 days. I left there after 1 am, the valet worried about aligning the car, and I desperate to leave.

In short: my cat is fine, hospitalization wasn't necessary, they tried to force hospitalization by charging me the full consultation fee even though it was a referral. I won't return and I won't recommend them simply because the clinic exploits a moment of vulnerability to make money; it lacks ethics!

My cat DIED in this hospital.
Now, in addition to dealing with grief, I have to deal with the irresponsible finance department of this place.
You can't leave this hospital without a release stating that everything is paid, regardless of your psychological state. They won't let you leave to breathe without EVERYTHING and then some being paid. After all, nothing is done in this place without them shoving papers in your face authorizing payment for procedures.
However, after paying almost 4,000 reais, my cat died a few hours later, so the costs were less than R$1,500.00. At the time, they told me I didn't need to deal with it, that I could go and arrange for the removal of my cat's body and the finance department would take care of the refund.
Both the veterinarian and the receptionist told me that there would be a refund since my cat didn't even stay the full day of hospitalization. It would be more than R$2,500 in reimbursement. The receptionist, of her own accord, gave me a statement of everything that had been done.

Ten days have passed and NO ONE has come to contact me. Besides going through the grieving process, I need to chase after this blessed refund, and as I said before, if it were the other way around, they wouldn't have even let me leave the hospital.
The problem is that after I questioned the refund, they told me they wouldn't do it because they performed procedures that weren't on the statement, procedures that I supposedly authorized through the family group, but I NEVER authorized anything there! When I asked for proof of this authorization, the attendant dodged the question, said it was just a figure of speech (???) and they continue to refuse to return the money.
The issue isn't so much about money, but gosh, I'm grieving and I have to deal with injustices! Now I'll have to find a lawyer to sue them.

Realistically, this hospital has many fixed costs and has no qualms about being abusive and extortionate.

This review serves as a message for those who cared for Syrup.
To the veterinarians at the Emergency Room, I want to express my immense gratitude for his final hours. I hesitated to leave this here or wondered if I should send it directly, but I chose to make it public with the main objective of perhaps generating reflection or change for other cases of aggressive lymphoma like that of our beloved Golden Retriever, who was only 6 years old.

"Samantha, you know that our Syrup passed away yesterday at the hospital where you work, at least it would be impossible not to know. I decided to follow the CHOP protocol guidelines, even though I was reluctant and afraid of causing him suffering, trusting your speech that medicine today is revolutionary and superior to that of years ago.
However, what I saw was, from the second week onwards, clear evidence of swelling of the eyelid, as well as, after that, of Syrup's tongue... an insistence on a standard protocol while Syrup was wasting away. The clear signs, even for us laypeople, showed that he needed an individualized approach. We know that there are extremely aggressive types of cancer, but precisely for that reason he needed specific attention, and not a ready-made formula that has proven ineffective. I know that there are protocol changes beyond the Immunohistochemical examination, which was only suggested in the third week — an examination with a deadline of 15 working days, which proved to be a late and ineffective suggestion given the state he was already in. Obviously, any in-depth investigation should have been proposed on the day 1.
However, if it's possible to worsen Syrup's story, the silence that followed his death contrasts sharply with the enthusiasm of the day the treatment was presented to us. While the emergency room welcomed us wonderfully, you didn't even send a message. Unfortunately, the modernity of medicine that you mentioned did not compensate for the lack of perception of his suffering and the emptiness in the support after his passing.

Having a renowned profession is useless if medicine is not accompanied by empathy and a keen eye for signs of suffering.

After consultations for my dog, I scheduled a combined surgery of 2 procedures with Dr. Ana Karine and Dr. Adriana Tomoko. I only have praise for Dr. Adriana Tomoko, but as for Dr. Ana Karine, stay away!

The surgery was scheduled for Monday, December 8th, since November 21st. On Friday the 5th, at 4 PM, her completely unprepared assistant contacted me claiming that I hadn't done one of the necessary exams, even though the doctor herself had already analyzed the exams during the consultation. He asked me to send the exams, even though they had already been sent to the doctor's number on November 21st. I sent the login and password, he took the wrong exams and said that it wouldn't be possible to do the surgery because they had already expired, even though the correct exams were very recent. He claimed the error was because I hadn't sent the exams in PDF format and had him access the portal, which is absurd considering that's his job. Dr. Ana Karine, still on Friday around 6 PM, completely unprepared, said she would confirm with the anesthesiologist if the blood tests could be accepted, as they were due one day before the surgery. And if they weren't accepted, what was I supposed to do on Friday at 6 PM with the surgery scheduled for Monday morning? A huge lack of respect; they could have noticed this detail beforehand. Furthermore, also on Friday night, they asked me to start medication on Saturday, which they could have sent beforehand along with all the preparations.

Dr. Ana Karine is extremely disorganized and completely rude. If I could, I would have gone back in time and canceled the surgery with her, but I was prioritizing my dog's health.

Today, 9 days post-surgery, I contacted them to schedule a follow-up appointment and they mentioned that they only see patients at Veros on Wednesdays. Without realizing it, I suggested the following Wednesday, which would fall on Christmas. She gave a very rude and stupid response: “I won’t be seeing patients on the 24th, Christmas Eve. Please contact Veros Hospital directly for a follow-up appointment.” She shouldn't be a doctor with this lack of skill in training her assistant, nor empathy and respect for pets and their owners.

Almost a month post-surgery, I was informed by Dr. Tomoko, who kindly provided me with the histopathological results, that in the ear where Dr. Ana Karine had performed the otoendoscopy, there were also foci of cholesteatoma. She had withheld this information from the day of the surgery and it was never passed on to me, even a month post-surgery!!!! She should be banned from the CRMV!

In addition to this case, the Veros hospital charged extra for items related to the surgery, such as R$1,600 for a blood bag in case a transfusion was needed. They didn't use the bag because a transfusion wasn't necessary; they justified this by saying the bag couldn't be returned to the chamber, and therefore the cost was passed on to the consumer – absurd! Dr. Tomoko informed me via WhatsApp that they hadn't administered a medication called Convenia, costing R$390.00, and that they would refund me, but they didn't! Upon discharge, they sent prescriptions for medications lacking basic information like GoV authentication and CRMV registration; I had to repeatedly ask them to send them correctly to be able to buy the medications. I'm staying away from this place.

I went to the Veros emergency room because my cat was feeling unwell. Upon arrival, the service was positive: the valet and reception staff were polite, welcoming, and efficient. The clinical evaluation also began appropriately.

However, when it came time to draw blood, the on-call doctor called two interns and asked, "Where do you think we should draw from?" This gave me a negative impression, as I expected the technical decisions to be made safely by experienced professionals. They decided, without asking or trying to understand how my cat usually reacts to these situations (which is basic in the handling of any animal, especially cats), that the blood would be drawn from the jugular vein.

When I questioned this option, the on-call doctor reacted with impatience, and the alternative was presented rudely, with the statement that another location "hurts more," instead of a clear technical explanation. The doctor's irritation was evident, and she even rolled her eyes. I was also informed of their intention to perform a "burrito" type restraint (wrapping the animal in a towel) without any prior context, attempt at a more careful approach, or understanding of my cat's behavior (which they knew would react very badly to this handling if they had bothered to ask).

Given the veterinarian's unwelcoming attitude and wanting to avoid subjecting my cat to inappropriate handling and unnecessary suffering, I chose to stop the appointment at that moment.

To make matters worse, while I was still in the hallway, I heard the doctor commenting, "It doesn't matter, she'll pay anyway," which I considered extremely inappropriate and incompatible with the professional conduct expected in a hospital setting (or any professional environment).

The customer service representative asked me about what happened in the hospital hallway as I was leaving and processed the refund, which made me think that the on-call veterinarian's behavior may not be consistent with Veros' overall conduct.

I ended up taking my cat to another feline-specialized emergency clinic, 4cats, where the experience was completely different. The staff were truly prepared to handle cats. Besides technical care, kindness, and professionalism, my cat was treated with respect and dignity, not like a mere guinea pig, which made all the difference in an emergency.

When we seek emergency care, we're already in a stressful situation, so the minimum expectation is to find an experienced team capable of conducting the care with skill and empathy. Unfortunately, my experience was exactly the opposite: I left Veros more stressed, more worried, and needing to rush to another emergency clinic.
Excellence
